items.title: The Download: inside the quest to make our minds immortal
items.raw_text: This is today’s edition of The Download , our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology. What we learned when our Roundtables explored the quest to make minds immortal To preserve our sense of self, some scientists are working on ways to keep our brains going—even beyond death. In their quest for cognitive immortality, these “mind savers” are exploring everything from head transplants and brain freezing to conscious software avatars. In the latest MIT Technology Review Roundtables event, senior editor for biomedicine Antonio Regalado joined science editor Mary Beth Griggs to examine these ideas. After following the money, the science, and the philosophy, he came back part skeptical, part awestruck. Here’s a taste of what Antonio found—and what he made of it. Not all the projects are quite what they seem: A $190 million US government program to develop replacement brain tissue is officially about treating stroke, but “it’s also a fig leaf for the actual ambition”: living forever. AI could lead to convincing mind clones: Large language models are making it possible to build AI copies of people that act quite like the real thing. “This digital avatar might not be good enough for you, but what if it’s good enough for me?” Immortality can be a hard sell: One company, Nectome, wants to preserve brains within 12 minutes of medically assisted death. “If you’re selling a hot product, this is not it.” It’s not always clear what we’re tr

items.title: Token fraud is here and it’s BAD (YouTube)
items.raw_text: Token fraud is here and it’s BAD (YouTube) Claire Vo runs ChatPRD , an AI platform that helps product managers "turn an idea into a spec". The product has been live since the GPT-4 era, and Claire has been building it in public for much of that time. In this YouTube video (see also the accompanying Twitter post ) Claire describes the flood of token fraud she has seen from groups abusing the product's free trial, sometimes just to get free AI usage but often to resell tokens or run other commercial enterprises on top of the ChatPRD agent. I am funding a international Roblox and Fortnite map studio. They run a loop of free trials and promo codes and then tunnel to my agent and use it to build Roblox and Fortnite maps. Apparently one of the common prompts Claire saw running through her agent involved SVGs of pelicans riding bicycles! Presumably the token scammers are using that to help sniff the underlying models - different model families have a definite signature, and I've used it like this in the past to try and guess the identity of stealth preview models on platforms like OpenRouter. Claire is winding down her free trials entirely, which sadly looks like the right decision in the face of this abuse. Tags: youtube , ai , generative-ai , llms , pelican-riding-a-bicycle , ai-misuse

items.title: PostgreSQL 19 Released
items.raw_text: PostgreSQL 19 Released Most years PostgreSQL ships a new release in September, but this year's release came two months later thanks mainly to the flurry of issues that the PostgreSQL team needed to address as part of the ongoing AI-reported vulnerability apocalypse. This release was definitely worth the wait. My favorite new feature is this one: For applications that send reads to standbys, PostgreSQL 19 adds "read-your-writes" consistency with the new WAIT FOR LSN command. A session on a standby can use WAIT FOR LSN to wait until the standby has replayed the write-ahead log (WAL) up to a specific log sequence number (LSN) before running a query, so the application can read data it just wrote on the primary. In practice, that looks like this: UPDATE movie SET genre = 'Dramatic' WHERE genre = 'Drama'; SELECT pg_current_wal_insert_lsn(); That returns a value like 0/0306EE20 . Store that somewhere (a signed cookie would work) such that on a subsequent request your application can do: WAIT FOR LSN '0/0306EE20' WITH (TIMEOUT '0.1s'); SELECT * FROM movie WHERE genre = 'Drama'; The timeout is optional - if you provide one you'll get an error if the replica you are talking to doesn't catch up within the specified time. I first encountered this pattern in Wikipedia , which has a hand-rolled version of this built against MySQL replication: In addition to this, MediaWiki attempts to ensure that the user sees events occurring on the wiki in chronological order. items.raw_text: Welcome to Edition 9.20 of the Rocket Report! Last weekend was a picture of the US launch business in miniature, and emblematic of the opposing trajectories of two of the nation's most experienced rocket makers. First, on Saturday, SpaceX completed a perfect midair catch of its Starship upper stage at its launch pad in Texas after spending nearly a day in orbit. The Super Heavy booster was lost at sea, but SpaceX proved it can recover that piece of the rocket on previous flights. While SpaceX showed it is well on the way to fielding a fully reusable rocket, United Launch Alliance suffered its first-ever total launch failure with the Vulcan rocket. That is terrible news for not only ULA, but also the US Space Force and Amazon, which have booked some 70 launches on Vulcan over the next few years. items.title: Trump admin still won't let Wi-Fi giant TP-Link sell its latest routers in US
items.raw_text: TP-Link, which may be the top provider of wireless routers for US homes and small businesses, isn't allowed to sell its latest Wi-Fi routers in the US. The Trump administration imposed a sweeping ban on foreign-made consumer routers in March 2026, and TP-Link hasn't been able to obtain an exemption. The rules prevent the import or sale of all new router models that are manufactured, assembled, designed, or developed outside the US. The Trump administration has control over which router makers receive special permission to import and sell new products through a waiver-review process involving the Federal Communications Commission, the Department of Defense, and the Department of Homeland Security. While some of its competitors have obtained exemptions to the ban, TP-Link appears to be having a hard time making its case to government officials. Its routers approved before the March 2026 ban remain available for sale in the US, but its newly released Wi-Fi 8 routers cannot be imported or sold. Read full article Comments

items.title: Maak kennis met Djuna: de schakel achter sterke bibliotheekcollecties
items.raw_text: Een collectie die aansluit bij de lokale gemeenschap, ruimte biedt aan verschillende perspectieven én bezoekers blijft verrassen. Het lijkt vanzelfsprekend als je door de bibliotheek loopt, maar achter de schermen komt daar veel bij kijken. Als adviseur collectie bij Rijnbrink helpt Djuna Bánki bibliotheken om weloverwogen keuzes te maken over hun collectie. Van boekhandel naar bibliotheekwereld Djuna werkt sinds augustus 2025 als adviseur collectie bij Rijnbrink. Haar liefde voor boeken en collectievorming ontstond al eerder. Na haar studie Nederlands werkte ze jarenlang in de boekhandel, waar ze verantwoordelijk was voor de non-fictieafdeling. ‘Ook daar was ik voortdurend bezig met vragen als: wie is onze doelgroep en welke boeken passen daarbij? Diezelfde afwegingen maak je in de bibliotheekwereld, maar dan vanuit een bredere maatschappelijke opdracht. Een goede collectie sluit aan bij de mensen die er gebruik van maken, maar maakt ook nieuwsgierig’, aldus Djuna. Meer dan alleen boeken Bibliotheekcollecties bestaan tegenwoordig uit veel meer dan alleen boeken. items.title: MAHA PAC spent more on steak, luxury club than candidates, report shows
items.raw_text: In the wake of the Make America Healthy Again movement's midterm wipeout , a top leader suggested the heavy losses came down to being outspent by wealthier, more powerful rivals. But a Stat report on MAHA's own spending in the run-up to the election raises questions about whether the group's priority was ever winning elections in the first place. The dive into the financial documents reveals that the MAHA PAC, led by Tony Lyons, spent more on allies, boosters, meals, luxuries, and its affiliated nonprofit than it did on political candidates. The findings are in stark contrast to an announcement from Lyons in the spring that he was heading a $100 million fundraiser to boost MAHA's clout in the midterms . In reality, MAHA PAC took in $3.2 million. During the election cycle, the PAC spent more than $10.5 million, with over $7 million coming from money it had collected previously. Read full article Comments

items.title: Man hired by Russia spied on Silicon Valley tech and defense company, feds say
items.raw_text: A Russian national has been indicted on suspicions he was a Russian spy who stalked and surveilled employees of a Silicon Valley company that was assisting Ukraine in its ongoing war with its eastern neighbor. Igor D’iu, 25, allegedly photographed the employees and their computer screens as they worked at a coffee shop located near the company’s Palo Alto office, federal prosecutors said Wednesday . He also kept a list of home addresses of employees and a senior executive. At one point, prosecutors said, D’iu trailed an employee as she traveled home from Palo Alto to San Francisco. An affidavit filed in the case referred to the employee as FEMP1, short for female employee, and said the event left her “in a state of emotional distress.” Evasive and irregular turns “FEMP1 made evasive and irregular turns, took back roads, and turned into a grocery store parking lot where D’IU continued aggressively following her vehicle,” an FBI special agent wrote. “D’IU followed FEMP1 through U-turns, illegal left turns, and ran a red light to stay with FEMP1 for nearly thirty miles. FEMP1 called 911 while driving and was instructed to drive directly to San Francisco Police Department (“SFPD”) Mission Station. Near SFPD Mission Station, FEMP1 flagged an SFPD patrol vehicle and reported the incident. D’IU left once FEMP1 made contact with the patrol vehicle.” Read full article Comments

items.title: Traumatized teens sue school, cops after Doritos bag triggers AI gun alert
items.raw_text: In October 2025, four Black high school students were sharing Cool Ranch Doritos after football practice, winding down and waiting for their rides home. It was then, in the lull of a moment any teen with after-school activities knows well, that the school’s AI gun detection system suddenly flagged one teen holding a bag of chips as a potential gunman. Within two minutes, Baltimore County Public Schools officials who reviewed security camera footage linked to the alert determined there was no actual threat. They recognized the Doritos bag and canceled the alert, which notified not only other school officials but also the Baltimore County Police Department that no response was needed. The false alert could have ended there—before a traumatizing campus clash with police—but it didn’t. Read full article Comments

items.title: Google turns to Blue Origin for a rocket, but its long-term problem remains
items.raw_text: Blue Origin announced Thursday that its New Glenn rocket will launch data center satellites for Google in 2029 as part of that company's Project Suncatcher program. Google disclosed it was working on scalable orbiting data centers about a year ago and characterized the project as one of its research "moonshots." The mission on New Glenn is designed to deploy satellites, each with computing capacity at roughly the scale of a data center rack, into Sun-synchronous orbit where they can receive nearly continuous solar energy. "Project Suncatcher is a long-term moonshot to scale AI infrastructure in space by tapping into the abundant solar power in orbit," said Travis Beals, senior director of Project Suncatcher at Google, in the news release. "This dedicated launch with Blue Origin represents a crucial milestone on our roadmap as we expand the boundaries of what's possible for the future of compute." Read full article Comments

items.title: "You’re right"—LLMs will get climate info wrong if you ask
items.raw_text: Many studies over the years have examined how people encounter climate science information. Some focused on the top results that Google surfaced (back when Google was still in the business of serving links), while others examined social media content or newspaper and TV news coverage. With large language models (LLMs) now forming a share of the public information diet, it's worth looking at how they handle climate change. But there’s no direct way for researchers to look at the information people have seen. It is served ephemerally to individual users, confined to their chat session. A study led by researchers from University College London and the United Nations Educational, Scientific, and Cultural Organization (UNESCO) tried to tackle this question from multiple angles, testing LLMs with different prompts and evaluating their output. They started with benchmarks of simple factual questions (benchmarks that might even be in models’ training data at this point) but also analyzed more complex interactions—including when users think they’re right to push back on an answer. CO 2 Q&A LLM research often faces ( no-true-Scotsman-tinged ) criticism for focusing on a particular model rather than some other frontier model that may have been released after the experiment concluded. In this case, the study used 33 models, including multiple versions of the major frontier and open-weight models. items.title: Google will launch Android app verification requirement globally in January 2027
items.raw_text: Google announced Android developer verification last year , and despite numerous objections from developers and users, the company is forging ahead . It began blocking the installation of unregistered apps in some countries this fall, and the system is expanding globally soon. Google says it will start rolling out the requirement in all regions in January 2027, and it urges devs who still haven't registered their apps to do so soon. The apps you download from the Play Store all come from verified developers, and Google's new requirement expands that requirement to apps from third-party sources. Once developer verification is live in your region, you won't be able to sideload apps unless the developer has registered with Google, which is framed as a security measure . Verification requires providing government identification and paying a $25 fee, which will allegedly make it harder for nefarious actors to distribute malware and scammy apps. In September, Google launched verification in Brazil, Indonesia, Singapore, and Thailand. Apparently, nothing exploded, so the company is now ready to expand. It previously said verification would go global in 2027, and it's not wasting any time with the January start. It says that verification will reach all devices within "several months." items.title: Mouse fight club might explain why we like to watch violent things
items.raw_text: Credit: J.M. Iravedra-Garcia et al., 2026 Credit: J.M. Iravedra-Garcia et al., 2026 There's something about watching violent events that broadly appeals to us, whether it's the latest John Wick movie, a video game, or a live UFC bout. Scientists have debated whether watching violent things could make us more aggressive, but it could also be an adaptive survival strategy. Male mice, for instance, who watched other mice fighting learned enough about how to fight to better protect themselves (compared to mice who didn't watch fights) when pitted against stronger, more aggressive opponents, according to a paper published in the journal Nature. The team randomly assigned male mice to three groups—fighters, spectators, or novices—and then subjected each group to eight days of training with three 10-minute sessions per day. The novices played with stuffed mice in isolation, while the spectators watched various pairs of fighter mice battle from a raised platform behind a transparent barrier—a set-up chosen to let them smell and listen to the fights as well as observe them. The ninth day was "fight night," when all the mice had to face a daunting opponent in three 4-minute rounds. Each fight was filmed from above so that the mouse behavior could be analyzed. To monitor corresponding changes in brain activity, the team engineered the rodents' excitatory brain cells to glow green whenever they were activated, while inhibitory brain cells glowed red. items.title: Show HN: Foolscap – a writing app that reads your book and never writes for you
items.raw_text: People are scared of their ability to write and think atrophying, so I wondered: what if I built something that enhanced human creativity instead of destroying it by doing the thinking and writing for people? Foolscap is the result, or at least the first version of that idea that's fleshed out enough to share here. It reads as you write and picks out the structure: characters, ideas, threads, what's left hanging. You can respond to what it picks out, so there's a dialectic between the system and you as the writer. There's also an agent on the side, plugged into the same system, so you can ask about your book and fire off actions through conversation. It never writes into your work. The system can also follow theorems and proofs and string together their dependencies, but I haven't made that a focus yet. There's no Lean support, for example. If anyone's interested in that, I'd love to hear it. I want to build this by iterating with the people who use it: a tool that uses AI not to bypass the creative process, but to bring new tools to it. There's a free tier, and if you email hello@foolscap.works I'll send you a code for 50% off. This is my first product, so feedback of any kind is welcome. Thanks, David

Het motto is ‘versnellen, versterken en vertrouwen’. Nederland moet technologie sneller kunnen toepassen en succesvolle innovaties laten doorgroeien. Daarvoor is een sterke digitale basis nodig, met voldoende mensen, kennis, ondernemerschap en infrastructuur. Tegelijkertijd vraagt digitalisering om vertrouwen in veilige technologie, digitale weerbaarheid en de vrijheid om bewuste keuzes te maken. NLdigital kijkt naar de voorwaarden waaronder bedrijven kunnen investeren in ai en andere digitale technologie, innoveren en internationaal opschalen. Daarbij staan de aantoonbare productiviteitswinst, maatschappelijke waarde en versterking van de concurrentiepositie centraal. De toekomstige welvaart en concurrentiekracht hangen volgens de branchevereniging in belangrijke mate af van het vermogen digitale technologie te ontwikkelen, gebruiken en op te schalen. items.title: Eén op de vijf Europese werknemers wordt gemonitord door software
items.raw_text: België monitort werknemers het meest, Nederland in bovenste helft Bijna één op de vijf Europese werknemers zegt dat een computerprogramma hun prestaties monitort. Bij 18 procent wijst software taken toe, bij 10 procent bepaalt ze de werktijden. België scoort opvallend hoog, Nederland zit in de bovenste helft van de EU. Dat blijkt uit een recent rapport van Eurofound , gebaseerd op de European Working Conditions Survey uit 2024. Het rapport meet algoritmisch management op basis van drie functies: prestatiemonitoring (software die bijhoudt hoe snel je tickets afhandelt), automatische taaktoewijzing (software die werk verdeelt) en automatische planning (software die je shifts inroostert). Algoritmisch management is volgens het rapport niet langer voorbehouden aan platformwerk, waarvan Uber-chauffeurs een bekend voorbeeld zijn. Het gebruik is het grootst in financiën en vastgoed, informatie en communicatie, en transport en opslag. Als je de drie vormen (monitoring, taaktoewijzing en planning) samen neemt, is de intensiteit in België na Denemarken het hoogst in de EU. Belgische werknemers krijgen dus vaker te maken met meerdere vormen van algoritmisch management tegelijk. Rekening houdend met verschillen in sector en beroep, zegt 31 procent van de Belgische werknemers dat hun prestaties worden gemonitord, het hoogste cijfer van de EU. items.title: Pilot Werkplaats Ontwerpende Aanpak: maak kennis met social designer Charlotte Grün
items.raw_text: Onlangs deelden we dat bij Bibliotheek De Lage Beemden een pilot is gestart als onderdeel van het project de Werkplaats Ontwerpende Aanpak . Met deze pilot onderzoekt SPN hoe de ontwerpende aanpak een vaste plek kan krijgen binnen bibliotheekorganisaties. Hiervoor gaat social designer Charlotte Grün in opdracht van SPN samen met medewerkers en directie aan de slag. Maar wie is Charlotte en hoe gaat zij als social designer te werk? Nieuwsgierigheid als vertrekpunt Een waslijn. Voor de meeste mensen een plek om natte kleding op te hangen. Voor Charlotte Grün aanleiding om iets te onderzoeken. Wat gebeurt er eigenlijk wanneer was droogt? Hoe kun je dat proces zichtbaar maken? Ze ontwierp een waslijn met gewichten en katrollen. Terwijl het water uit de kleding verdampte, werd de was lichter en kwam de constructie langzaam in beweging. Het droogproces werd zichtbaar en hoorbaar. Die nieuwsgierigheid typeert Charlotte.
